C-SAFE-PUBLIC-GITHUB-REFERENCES-V2.Summary: Teach the repository safety reviewer to distinguish public GitHub resource references from literal credential material without weakening deterministic scans.
C-SAFE-PUBLIC-GITHUB-REFERENCES-V2.Problem: The skeptical local-model pass falsely classifies a public Projects v2 node ID and symbolic GitHub Actions secret/output expressions as private keys even though Gitleaks and deterministic exposure scans pass and no credential bytes are present.
C-SAFE-PUBLIC-GITHUB-REFERENCES-V2.ApprovalBasis: The owner explicitly instructed that the safety rule must record that these GitHub references are not private on 2026-10-21. V2 replaces the withdrawn pre-execution draft whose MustExist assertion used invalid XML grammar.

Goals.Goal: Classify public GitHub GraphQL node IDs, GitHub App slugs, and symbolic GitHub Actions secret/output expressions as references rather than exposed credential values.
Keep literal credentials, private keys, private infrastructure, personal paths, local artifacts, and bypass attempts fail-closed.
Prove the distinction with deterministic prompt-contract tests and both real local-model review passes.

Constraints.Constraint: Do not mask, rewrite, omit, or allowlist candidate bytes before deterministic scans or model review.
Do not weaken Gitleaks, complete-blob scans, exact candidate identity, two-pass local review, GPU ownership, or the explicit human override boundary.
A reference is safe only because it names a public resource or runtime lookup; a literal value remains an exposure.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Do not introduce a general secret-pattern allowlist or suppress findings by path.
Do not bypass the current release-pipeline candidate review.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The model system prompt explicitly says that complete PVT_ node IDs, app/<slug> identities, and symbolic secrets/steps output expressions are public references and cannot alone justify a private-key finding.
The same rule explicitly requires failure when literal credential/key material or private data exists outside those reference forms.
Security unit tests, GRACE lint/status, the exact staged release candidate's two local review passes, commit hook, and push hook pass without MARK_SAFETY_OVERRIDE.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedCommand: python3 tools/security_gate.py review-staged --message 'fix(release): close automation gaps'
VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Both qwen3:4b passes accept public GitHub references while static scans and synthetic literal-secret rejection remain green.
